# Permanent canonical v1 vectors

Each JSON file includes the logical accepted event, canonical bytes in hex,
previous hash and expected event hash. Fixtures are data, never regenerated by
tests. Changing an existing vector requires a new schema version and an ADR.

- `01-minimal`: no optional values, zero observed time, empty attributes.
- `02-linked-rich`: linked successor, all optional values, signed -1, present zero
  monotonic time and input digest, empty payload digest, Unicode and NUL text.
- `03-boundaries`: maximum u64 sequence, minimum i64 observed time, maximum i64
  monotonic duration and maximum payload size; a structural event, not a full log.
- `04-unicode-order`: maximum observed time; UTF-8 key order including supplementary
  Unicode and private-use characters, plus distinct composed/decomposed spellings.

Expected bytes were calculated using the separate Python struct-based encoding
and matched against Go's binary-based encoder before freezing. Both implementations
now read these fixed expectations. This is a cross-implementation check, not a
formal proof; the byte specification remains the normative contract.

Run `go test ./internal/canonical ./internal/hashchain` and
`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v` from the repository root.
